test_title: PYST 5: SSC Stenographer - English (Held On:18 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The scholar of the department could help the junior students in the proposed coaching.

options.text: The junior students could be helped by the scholar of the department in the proposed coaching.
The junior students could have been helped by the scholar of the department in the proposed coaching.
The junior students could have helped by the scholar of the department in the proposed coaching.
The junior students can help by the scholar of the department in the proposed coaching.

solution:
The **correct answer** is 'Option 1' i.e., *'The junior students could be helped by the scholar of the department in the proposed coaching.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The task here is to convert the sentence from **active to passive voice** without changing its original meaning.
 
• The **original sentence structure** has the subject 'The scholar of the department' performing the action **'could help'** on the object 'the junior students'.
 
• **In converting **to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the subject of the active sentence becomes the agent that performs the action.
 
• So, **'The junior students**' becomes the subject of the sentence,** 'could be helped' **is the passive form of the verb, and 'by the scholar of the department' is indicating who is performing the action.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is** 'Option 1'.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2** *('The junior students could have been helped by the scholar of the department in the proposed coaching')* changes the tense of the verb, from could help (which has an uncertain future connotation) to could have helped (which refers to an opportunity in the past that was missed).
 
• **Option 3*** ('The junior students could have helped by the scholar of the department in the proposed coaching') *not only changes the tense but also disrupts the sentence structure making it grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 4*** ('The junior students can help by the scholar of the department in the proposed coaching.')* is simply incorrect in structure and meaning. 'Can help' is not the correct conversion from 'could help' and the overall structure is not grammatically correct.
